choices.text: The equilibrium shifts toward the products, so more product is made at equilibrium
The equilibrium shifts toward the reactants, to cancel the catalyst out
Equilibrium is reached sooner, but the position of equilibrium and Kc are unchanged, because both rates speed up equally
Nothing changes at all, because a catalyst is never used up

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: A catalyst pushes the equilibrium toward the products. A faster forward reaction looks like the products are winning. A catalyst speeds the forward and reverse reactions equally: the position of equilibrium is unchanged. It lowers the activation energy for both directions, so the mixture gets to the same equilibrium faster.
questions.misconception: A catalyst pushes the equilibrium toward the products.
questions.prompt: A reversible reaction sits at equilibrium and a catalyst is added. A student claims the equilibrium now makes more product. What actually happens?

questions.explanation: Bond enthalpies: energy in to break H-H and Cl-Cl is 436 + 242 = 678 kJ mol-1; energy out forming two H-Cl bonds is 2 x 431 = 862 kJ mol-1. ΔH = in - out = 678 - 862 = -184 kJ mol-1, and the negative sign means exothermic.
questions.prompt: For H2 + Cl2 -> 2 HCl, with bond enthalpies H-H 436, Cl-Cl 242 and H-Cl 431 kJ mol-1, what is the enthalpy change of the reaction?

questions.answer: In = 436 + 193 = 629 kJ mol-1; out = 2 x 366 = 732 kJ mol-1; ΔH = 629 - 732 = -103 kJ mol-1. The reaction is exothermic.
questions.explanation: ΔH is energy in to break bonds minus energy out when bonds form: 629 - 732 = -103 kJ mol-1. A negative ΔH means the products lie below the reactants, as in scene s1.
questions.prompt: Using bond enthalpies H-H 436, Br-Br 193 and H-Br 366 kJ mol-1, calculate the enthalpy change for H2 + Br2 -> 2 HBr, showing your working, and state whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

questions.explanation: The Kc expression puts products over reactants, each raised to its stoichiometric power: numerator 0.16, denominator 0.20 x 0.216 = 0.0432, giving Kc = 3.70 - the value a catalyst cannot change, because it speeds both rates equally.
questions.prompt: For N2 + 3 H2 <-> 2 NH3 at equilibrium, [N2] = 0.20, [H2] = 0.60 and [NH3] = 0.40 mol dm-3. Calculate Kc, showing the expression you use.

choices.text: Every molecule moves faster at the higher temperature, so every collision reacts
The distribution flattens and shifts right, so a larger fraction of molecules has energy at least Ea and more collisions per second can react
The activation energy falls as the temperature rises, so the barrier is easier to clear
The molecules collide less often but each collision is stronger

questions.explanation: On the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve the area past Ea grows at higher temperature: the distribution flattens and shifts right while Ea itself stays fixed. More molecules can react on collision, so the rate rises - exactly the morph in scene s4.
